main_body: Bare gothic dead tree: a trunk with a flared root base and branching limbs, with crows perched in the branches
top_band: none. The trunk column reads as a continuous dark brown run from row 33 to row 62 with no lighter horizontal surface. The organic form has no top surface to show.
evidence: The drawing is an organic bare tree: a vertical trunk, branches and a small flat base. It has no horizontal top surface to judge, and none of the contract's failure types (front-elevation cabinet, rim-only column, top-down slab) applies to a tree. The trunk column is one continuous dark brown run. The branches are thin diagonal limbs, so no top band is needed. For organic kinds the silhouette reads as a natural tree seen from the front, with nothing visibly wrong in the 3/4 view.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 11 distinct colours and a median of 7 colours per tile. The references have 427 and 567 colours and a median of about 108 per tile. 93% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is near-black and reads as the sticker look, whereas the references have tinted outlines (0% neutral). The trunk has about 4 brown steps with a little bark grain, and the limbs are mostly 2-3 tone strips. Next to the leafy, richly shaded references it looks much thinner and flatter. The bare, dark look is a palette choice and is not penalised, but the shading depth, outline tint and tile density are far below the bar.
